issues.legal_issue: A building owner may seek eviction on a statutory ground of personal requirement or rent default even when another person has acted as landlord by collecting rent.
material_facts: The claimant relied on an exchange deed establishing ownership of the premises, and the tenant did not dispute that ownership.
The former owner had collected rent and represented himself as landlord, including after the ownership transfer.
The tenant had approached the claimant to pay rent, but the claimant refused to accept it; the tenant also paid electricity and other charges to the claimant.
The claimant sought eviction for personal use of the premises and for non-payment of rent.
issues.conclusion: The statutory definition of landlord is broad, and the former owner's collection of rent did not prevent the owner from seeking eviction on the grounds of personal requirement or rent default. The High Court erred in finding no landlord-tenant relationship on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(c) of the Assam Urban Areas Rent Control Act, 1972 defines landlord broadly to include a person receiving or entitled to receive rent, including on behalf of another. Under Section 5, eviction may be sought on specified grounds, including bona fide requirement and non-payment of rent. For a claim based on the landlord's own personal requirement, the claimant must be an owner entitled to occupy the building in their own right; a mere rent collector cannot claim personal occupation. M.M. Quasim v. Manohar Lal Sharma & Ors., AIR 1981 SC 113, applied that distinction under a comparable rent-control statute.

rule.if: statutory_rent_eviction_proceeding and claimant_owns_building and another_person_collected_rent and (claimant_seeks_personal_occupation or claimant_alleges_rent_default)

predicates.statutory_rent_eviction_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding under a rent-control law seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.claimant_owns_building: The claimant owns the building and is entitled to occupy it in their own right.
predicates.another_person_collected_rent: Another person collected rent from the tenant or acted as the landlord in relation to the tenancy.
predicates.claimant_seeks_personal_occupation: The claimant seeks possession for their own bona fide occupation.
predicates.claimant_alleges_rent_default: The claimant alleges that the tenant failed to pay rent lawfully due.

issues.definition: If an owner seeks eviction in a rent-control proceeding for personal occupation or alleged rent default, another person's collection of rent does not by itself prevent the owner from seeking eviction.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee of a lessor's interest obtains the lessor's rights and liabilities under an existing tenancy without the tenant's attornment.
material_facts: The original owner transferred the property interest to the claimant while the tenancy already existed.
The tenant had not attorned to the claimant, but had approached the claimant to pay rent and paid electricity and other charges to the claimant.
The lower courts had not considered the effect of the transfer on the tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The transfer vested the claimant with the lessor's rights and liabilities concerning the existing tenancy without requiring the tenant to attorn; the absence of attornment did not prevent the claimant from seeking eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 109 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 provides that a transferee of leased property or an interest in it obtains the lessor's rights and, subject to the statutory terms, liabilities concerning the subsisting tenancy. Attornment by the tenant is not a condition for the transfer of those rights to take effect.

predicates.existing_tenancy: A lease or tenancy is in existence when the lessor transfers an interest in the leased property.
predicates.lessor_transfers_interest: The lessor transfers the leased property or an interest in it to another person.
predicates.transferee_seeks_lessor_rights: The transferee seeks to exercise the lessor's rights concerning the existing tenancy.

issues.definition: When a lessor transfers an interest in property subject to an existing tenancy, a transferee seeking the lessor's rights succeeds to them without the tenant's attornment.
